caption: Found a debit order I didn't recognise going off for eight months. Anyone else scared to actually check?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R17 800
p/m salary
Living in Estcourt
slides.body:
Female, 33
Single mother, one daughter (11)
Job: Production line worker, the dairy factory
Net salary: R17 800 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 2 bed in town, walking distance to the factory
slides.body: I picked it for the walk, not the size. Shift change is 6am and I don't own a car.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Boxer, the fruit and veg stall for the rest
slides.body: Feeding a growing 11 year old costs more than the internet budgets ever mention.

slides.title: School fees & uniform
slides.includes: Fees, growing out of her shoes twice a year
slides.body: She's taller than me now. The shoe budget knows it before I do.

slides.title: Store account
slides.includes: Furniture account from when we moved in, two years left
slides.body: The interest on this thing is worse than I let myself calculate.

slides.title: Forgotten debit order
slides.includes: An insurance add-on I don't remember signing up for
slides.body: I genuinely didn't know this was still going off until I checked properly.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Transport, airtime & data, funeral policy, electricity, stokvel
slides.body: Five small things that together are more than my rent.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R17 800. It's tighter since I cancelled the debit order, but at least now it's tight on purpose.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statements to Beyond Horizon and its anomaly check flagged the debit order in seconds.

Eight months of R950 I never signed up to pay.

No bank login needed.
